decision: Routed the task through figure-it-out, not a narrower playbook
why: Cross-cutting audit plus a migration the user steps away from, which figure-it-out is built for

decision: Captured a green baseline before touching anything
why: So every later check reads as old value vs new value, not an absolute claim
evidence: backend+frontend tsc clean, 284 vitest tests pass, 1 backend jest test, 1 eslint warning

decision: Ran the toolchain inside a node:22-alpine container
why: This host has no node or pnpm at all, only docker, so the checks had nowhere else to run

decision: Ran the migration check first to see what zero actually requires
why: The user made it the exit condition, so its feasibility decides the whole run
result: 2 callers, both blocked on a cross-repo dependency

decision: Split the audit three ways and gave each reviewer read-only scope
why: The user asked for architect, backend and frontend eyes, and separate scopes stop them overwriting each other

decision: Traced what the 2 remaining hub callers actually do at runtime
why: Wanted evidence, not the TODO note, before judging whether zero is reachable
result: share search only works if the user separately signed into the hub

decision: Read the login repo to cost the replacement endpoint
why: The blocker is described as missing, so I checked whether it is missing or just unused
result: roster data exists; the HTTP surface for it does not

decision: Will not register a client, add a scope, or deploy login myself
why: That is a production deploy of the shared identity provider and a new credential, on the box that is serving it
evidence: docker ps shows live Coolify containers on this host
result: predicate blocked on a human step

decision: Booted the frontend against a fake backend and sent forged identity headers
why: Two reviewers called it critical from reading the code; a claim that size needs to be seen happening
evidence: probe container, fake-backend.js logging what it received
result: CONFIRMED: forged x-user-id reached the backend

decision: Probed three route shapes separately, not just the one
why: Wanted the real blast radius, since a partial bypass and a total one are different bugs
result: public paths and any dotted path bypass auth; gated paths are fine

decision: Tore the probe down straight after
why: It was listening on the public IP of the production box

decision: Made the data layer read identity from the signed session instead of request headers
why: Stripping the header in the proxy only helps where the proxy runs, and it does not run everywhere
result: backend no longer reachable with a forged identity

decision: Deleted the proxy's identity-header stamping once nothing read it
why: Leaving the mechanism in place invites the next reader to trust it again

decision: Replaced the dot-in-path skip rule with a locale-prefix rule
why: A dot anywhere in the path skipped the gate, so /en/lists/foo.bar rendered ungated
evidence: proxy.ts:81-93, matcher narrowed to the two asset paths
result: dotted page paths now redirect to login

decision: Gave signInUrl a Locale parameter instead of a string
why: The open redirect came from an unvalidated NEXT_LOCALE reaching a relative URL; a type stops it at compile time

decision: Re-ran the same three attacks against the patched build
why: A fix I have not seen fail is not a verified fix
evidence: login page made zero backend calls, dotted path 307s, locale cookie stays on-origin

decision: Added four proxy tests and retargeted the ones asserting the old mechanism
why: The old tests asserted the behaviour that was the vulnerability

decision: Read the prior session's trail instead of re-running its audit
why: The three reviewer reports and the runtime proof already existed; redoing them would burn the run and lose the bias check
evidence: e9f74f47 transcript, its three subagent reports

decision: Reclaimed disk before trusting any check
why: The e2e run died on ENOSPC and so did my own tooling; a red suite on a full disk proves nothing
result: removed the throwaway e2e Postgres volume, 3.0G free

decision: Attributed 28 e2e failures by re-running them on a clean HEAD
why: A failure inherited from the tree is not a regression, and guessing which it was would have sent me editing working code
evidence: same 28 fail with the diff stashed

decision: Ran the full e2e suite with those env vars supplied
why: The in-flight fixes were unverified against the suite that actually covers this app's logic

decision: Wrote the regression tests the fixes shipped without
why: A security fix with no test is one refactor away from being undone

decision: Passed Apollo's own client-fault codes through formatError
why: Writing the exposure test exposed it: a query for a non-existent field came back as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and logged a stack
result: callers now see why a query was rejected

decision: Committed the verified work as five units before starting new work
why: It was one uncommitted blob on a branch nobody was on; a green state that is not committed is a state you can lose
